option_description: Attests the CA corroborates ACME http-01/dns-01 domain-control validation from >=2 geographically distant vantage points (Multi-Perspective Issuance Corroboration, CA/Browser Forum SC-067), so a localized BGP/DNS hijack reaching one validator cannot forge a passing challenge.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Spoofable ACME domain-control validation" — fires when this is false (single-vantage validation), letting a BGP/DNS hijack of the one validator mint a cert for a domain the attacker does not control. MPIC is the network-leg defense paired with CAA binding and DNSSEC.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Have the CA operator attest whether Multi-Perspective Issuance Corroboration is enabled. Public CAs are required to per SC-067; self-hosted/single-vantage step-ca typically validates from one vantage — record as residual risk and pair with EAB + CAA.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CA operator attests MPIC is enabled (>=2 remote vantage points corroborate). Single-vantage step-ca = residual risk, set false.
how_to_obtain.source: CA/Browser Forum Ballot SC-067 / Let's Encrypt multi-vantage-point validation (USENIX Security '21)

option_description: Attests the domain publishes CAA records (RFC 8657) with accounturi= (bind issuance to one ACME account) and validationmethods= (restrict the permitted domain-control method, e.g. dns-01 only), and that the CA honors them.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Spoofable ACME domain-control validation" — fires when false (no CAA account/method binding), so a hijacked vantage can pass an unauthorized method and a stolen account elsewhere can mint certs for the domain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the domain's CAA records and confirm accounturi= and validationmethods= parameters are present.
how_to_obtain.command: dig +short CAA example.com
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 0 issue "<ca-host>; accounturi=https://<ca>/acme/acct/1234; validationmethods=dns-01" (secure) vs no CAA / bare issue with no params (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8657 (accounturi / validationmethods CAA parameters)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the ACME provisioner publishes its caaIdentities so clients can pin CAA against the CA's issuer-domain-name.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | select(.type=="ACME") | .caaIdentities'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: caaIdentities populated so the CA's issuer-domain-name is published for clients to set CAA against
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (caaIdentities JSON field)

option_description: Attests the domain's DNS is DNSSEC-signed and the CA performs DNSSEC validation when resolving the dns-01 TXT record and the CAA lookup, so an off-path DNS hijack/cache-poisoning cannot forge the challenge TXT or strip CAA undetected.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Spoofable ACME domain-control validation" — fires when false. DNSSEC is the third leg (alongside MPIC and CAA binding) that closes single-vantage domain-control spoofing of the dns-01 challenge and CAA lookup.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the enrollment domain is DNSSEC-signed by checking for DS/RRSIG records and an authenticated-data response from a validating resolver.
how_to_obtain.command: dig +dnssec example.com SOA; dig DS example.com
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RRSIG records and a DS record present, resolver returns the 'ad' (authenticated-data) flag = DNSSEC validated (secure); no DS/RRSIG = unsigned zone (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the CA's own resolver performs DNSSEC validation when resolving the dns-01 TXT and CAA lookups (not just that the zone is signed).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CA operator attests the validating resolver enforces DNSSEC for challenge/CAA resolution; a non-validating resolver leaves the dns-01 path spoofable.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attests the enrollment flow requires the requesting client to authenticate before issuance (ACME EAB, EST mTLS / HTTP-Basic-over-TLS, or a per-device SCEP secret), so no path mints certificates for an unauthenticated caller.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak enrollment authentication / open issuance oracle" — fires when false: any party that can reach the endpoint (ACME finalize, EST simpleenroll, SCEP) can mint certificates, an unauthenticated issuance oracle.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe each enrollment path (EST simpleenroll, ACME finalize, SCEP) without credentials and confirm it rejects the request before issuance.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -k https://<est-host>/.well-known/est/simpleenroll -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'  # expect 401/handshake-fail without client cert
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Without credentials: TLS handshake requires a client cert OR 401 (secure). 200/enroll succeeding unauthenticated on any path = insecure (set false).
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 7030 §3.3/§3.2 (TLS client auth, server MUST be authenticated, NULL/anon forbidden)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm no enrollment path (ACME finalize, EST simpleenroll, SCEP) accepts a request without authenticating the client first.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Operator confirms every enrollment endpoint gates issuance on client authentication; any open path sets this false.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attests the ACME provisioner requires External Account Binding (RFC 8555 externalAccountBinding; step-ca --require-eab / requireEAB:true), tying account creation to a pre-issued MAC key/keyID so only pre-authorized clients can enroll.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak enrollment authentication / open issuance oracle" — fires when false: ACME account creation is open and anyone passing a domain challenge can obtain a cert from the internal CA.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the ACME provisioner's requireEAB flag and confirm a managed EAB key list exists; verify account creation rejects requests lacking a valid externalAccountBinding.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | select(.type=="ACME") | .requireEAB'; step ca acme eab list <provisioner>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: requireEAB: true and a managed EAB key list (secure). Add via: step ca provisioner add <name> --type ACME --require-eab; step ca acme eab add <provisioner> <ref>
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners / step ca acme eab add reference (--require-eab flag, eab add command)

option_description: Attests the EST endpoint (RFC 7030) requires TLS client-certificate authentication (or HTTP-Basic/Digest strictly over TLS) for simpleenroll, with the server authenticated in the handshake and no NULL/anon ciphers.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak enrollment authentication / open issuance oracle" — fires when false: the EST endpoint accepts unauthenticated enrollment requests, an open issuance oracle.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Hit EST /simpleenroll without a client certificate and confirm the handshake demands a cert or the server returns 401.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -k https://<est-host>/.well-known/est/simpleenroll -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'  # expect 401/handshake-fail without client cert
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Without a client cert: TLS handshake requires cert OR 401 (secure). 200/enroll succeeding unauthenticated = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 7030 §3.3/§3.2 (TLS client auth, server MUST be authenticated, NULL/anon forbidden)

option_description: Attests the SCEP provisioner authenticates enrollment with a single static, long-lived, broadly-distributed shared challenge password rather than a dynamic per-device/one-time secret. A leaked or sniffed static challenge lets an attacker enroll arbitrary devices.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak enrollment authentication / open issuance oracle" — fires when true (static shared secret in use). Secure value is false (dynamic per-enrollment challenge).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SCEP provisioner challenge: a single literal shared challenge string across all devices sets this true; a dynamic per-device one-time challenge sets it false.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | select(.type=="SCEP") | {challengeStatic: (.challenge!=null), encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier, minimumPublicKeyLength}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A single literal 'challenge' string shared across devices = static-secret finding (true). A dynamic per-device one-time challenge = false.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (SCEP challenge / encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier default 0=DES-CBC / minimumPublicKeyLength default 2048)

option_description: True when the CA constrains the requester-supplied CSR Subject/SAN/EKU to the identity the enrollment principal is authorized for (x509 name policy, certificate template, or disableCustomSANs on cloud provisioners) rather than blindly honoring whatever the CSR asks for.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Requester-supplied SAN/Subject honored at issuance" — fires when false (the ESC1-analogue): a low-privilege enrollee can mint a certificate impersonating any host or user. step-ca X5C/JWK provisioners issue for ANY Subject by default unless a template/name-policy restricts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect each provisioner for an x509 template / allow-deny name policy bounding SANs, and check cloud provisioners for disableCustomSANs. Absent template on X5C/JWK = unconstrained.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {type, claims, options}'; cat <template>.tpl
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Provisioner carries an x509 template / allow-deny name policy bounding SANs; cloud provisioner shows disableCustomSANs:true (sets true). Absent template + X5C/JWK = unconstrained, ESC1-style (false).
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (disableCustomSANs, X5C 'any Subject names' + templates) / EJBCA Certificate Profile Fields (Allow Subject DN Override risk)

option_description: True when the provisioner accepts arbitrary requester-chosen SANs with no allow/deny bound — disableCustomSANs is off on a cloud provisioner, or an X5C/JWK provisioner has no SAN-bounding template. Captures the disableCustomSANs control point from the insecure polarity.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Requester-supplied SAN/Subject honored at issuance" — fires when true (custom SANs unconstrained). Secure value is false (custom SANs disabled / bounded). Distinct polarity from enrollee_supplies_subject_disabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether the provisioner accepts arbitrary requester SANs: disableCustomSANs off / no bounding template sets this true.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {type, claims, options}'; cat <template>.tpl
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Cloud provisioner with disableCustomSANs:false, or X5C/JWK with no SAN-bounding template = true (unconstrained). disableCustomSANs:true / bounding template = false.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (disableCustomSANs, X5C 'any Subject names' + templates) / EJBCA Certificate Profile Fields (Allow Subject DN Override risk)

option_description: True when an x509 certificate template or allow/deny name policy is attached to the enrollment provisioner that bounds the allowed DNS/IP SANs, Subject DN, and EKU per authorized identity.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Requester-supplied SAN/Subject honored at issuance" — fires when false (the absent-template X5C/JWK case), so the CA honors arbitrary Subject/SAN. Secondary trigger for the ESC1-analogue weakness from the policy-enforcement angle.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a certificate template or x509 allow/deny name policy is bound to the provisioner, bounding SAN/Subject/EKU per identity.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {type, claims, options}'; cat <template>.tpl
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An x509 template / allow-deny name policy is present and bound (true); no template/policy on the provisioner = false (unconstrained).
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (disableCustomSANs, X5C 'any Subject names' + templates) / EJBCA Certificate Profile Fields (Allow Subject DN Override risk)

option_description: Which provisioner mints certificates on this enrollment flow (acme/scep/est/jwk/oidc/x5c/cloud). Context for interpreting the SAN/Subject constraint: X5C/JWK default to 'any Subject', cloud provisioners expose disableCustomSANs, ACME finalize honors the CSR SANs.
security_impact: Not itself a trigger. Provides context for "Requester-supplied SAN/Subject honored at issuance" — disambiguates which constraint mechanism (template, disableCustomSANs, CSR honoring) the assessor must check.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Record the provisioner type(s) from step-ca config to scope which constraint mechanism applies.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {name, type}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List of provisioners with type one of acme/scep/est/jwk/oidc/x5c/cloud, identifying the enrollment mechanism in use.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (challenges JSON field)

option_description: Whether the certificate private key traverses the enrollment channel (server-side keygen with PKCS#12 key delivery). True = the issued private key is on the wire and in CA memory; secure (false) keeps the private key client-side so only the CSR/public key crosses the channel.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Issued private key exposed in transit" — fires when true: the private key is on the wire and in CA memory, exposed to MITM and CA compromise.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether the CA generates the keypair and returns the private key (PKCS#12) on the wire, or only the public key (CSR) crosses the channel.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enrollment client attests keypair is generated locally (ACME/EST simple-enroll, SCEP PKCSReq carry a client CSR) = false. Any server-side-keygen / PKCS#12-with-key delivery path = true.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8555 (CSR-based finalize) / RFC 7030 §4.2 (simpleenroll with client CSR) / general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the requesting host generates the keypair locally and submits a CSR carrying only the public key (RFC 8555 finalize / RFC 7030 simpleenroll). Secure value is true.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Issued private key exposed in transit" — fires when false, because the CA generates the key and returns it (PKCS#12 with private key in transit / resident at the CA).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the enrollee generates its keypair locally and submits only a CSR; CA-side keygen with PKCS#12 return sets this false.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enrollment client attests keypair is generated locally (ACME/EST simple-enroll, SCEP PKCSReq carry a client CSR) = true. Any server-side-keygen / PKCS#12-with-key delivery path = false.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8555 (CSR-based finalize) / RFC 7030 §4.2 (simpleenroll with client CSR) / general-knowledge

option_description: The SCEP encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier used to wrap the PKCS#7 enrollment payload (step-ca default 0 = DES-CBC). des_cbc/3des_cbc provide no real confidentiality for an issued private key carried in the SCEP response; secure value is aes256_cbc (encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier=2).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Issued private key exposed in transit" — fires when the weak DES/3DES algorithms are selected, so a SCEP response carrying private material has no real confidentiality.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the SCEP provisioner encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier; 0/1 (DES/3DES-CBC) are weak, 2 (aes256_cbc) is secure. Default is 0=DES-CBC and must be overridden.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | select(.type=="SCEP") | {challengeStatic: (.challenge!=null), encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier, minimumPublicKeyLength}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier:2 (aes256_cbc) = secure. Default 0 (DES-CBC) / 1 (3DES-CBC) = weak finding.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (SCEP challenge / encryptionAlgorithmIdentifier default 0=DES-CBC / minimumPublicKeyLength default 2048)

option_description: Attests the certificate-enrollment flow is carried exclusively over TLS/HTTPS (ACME mandates HTTPS per RFC 8555 §6.1; EST mandates TLS 1.1+ per RFC 7030 §3.3). When false, legacy SCEP plain-HTTP enrollment or an http:// directory exposes CSRs, SCEP challenge-passwords, and issued material.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext enrollment transport" — fires when false (any plain-HTTP enrollment path), exposing enrollment material to network interception and tampering.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the ACME directory is served only over HTTPS and that no plain-HTTP enrollment endpoint responds.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <ca-host>:443 -alpn acme-tls/1 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject; curl -sI http://<ca-host>/acme/<provisioner>/directory
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACME directory served only over HTTPS (secure); plain-HTTP SCEP endpoint responding 200 on http:// = insecure cleartext enrollment
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8555 §6.1 (HTTPS required) / step-ca acme-basics (ACME API requires HTTPS)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the EST endpoint negotiates TLS 1.1+ with no NULL/anon cipher.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <est-host>:443 -tls1_2 </dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EST endpoint negotiates TLS 1.1+ with no NULL/anon cipher (secure). RFC 7030 forbids NULL/anon suites and mandates TLS for HTTP Basic/Digest.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 7030 §3.3 (HTTPS MUST, TLS 1.1+, NULL/anon MUST NOT)

option_description: Interpreted attestation that the enrollment endpoint negotiates NULL or anonymous (aNULL/eNULL) TLS cipher suites, which provide no confidentiality and/or no server authentication. RFC 7030 §3.3 forbids NULL/anon suites for EST.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext enrollment transport" — fires when true: an enrollment TLS session accepting NULL/anon suites is effectively cleartext-equivalent and MITM-able. Secure value is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test-negotiate the enrollment endpoint for aNULL/eNULL suites; any acceptance sets this true.
how_to_obtain.command: testssl.sh --cipher-per-proto https://<ca-host>:443 | grep -iE 'null|anon'; openssl s_client -connect <ca-host>:443 -cipher 'aNULL:eNULL' </dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No NULL/anon cipher negotiated (handshake fails) = secure (false). Any aNULL/eNULL suite accepted = true (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 7030 §3.3 (HTTPS MUST, TLS 1.1+, NULL/anon MUST NOT)

option_description: Minimum TLS protocol version the enrollment transport will negotiate. EST requires TLS 1.1+; modern hardening expects TLS 1.2+. A floor of SSLv3/TLS1.0 permits downgraded, weakly-protected enrollment sessions.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext enrollment transport" — fires on legacy/insecure floor values (SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1). Secure value is TLS1.2 or TLS1.3.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the lowest TLS version the enrollment endpoint will negotiate by probing each protocol floor.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <ca-host>:443 -tls1 </dev/null; openssl s_client -connect <ca-host>:443 -tls1_2 </dev/null; testssl.sh -p https://<ca-host>:443
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handshake fails for SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 and succeeds at TLS1.2+ = secure. A successful SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 handshake reveals the insecure floor.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 7030 §3.3 (HTTPS MUST, TLS 1.1+, NULL/anon MUST NOT)

option_description: Attests that JWK/OIDC/X5C provisioner enrollment tokens (bearer JWTs that authorize cert issuance) are short-lived and single-use. When false, a stolen or replayed long-lived reusable token mints trusted certs at will, bypassing challenge validation.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Provisioner / enrollment-token compromise" — fires when false (long-lived/reusable token). Secure value is true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate JWK/OIDC/X5C provisioners and confirm token TTL is short and tokens are single-use (nonce enforced); long-lived or replayable tokens set this false.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {name,type}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enumerate JWK/OIDC/X5C provisioners; confirm token TTL is short, tokens are bound (sub/sans/sha), and single-use. Long-lived/replayable tokens = false.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (JWK token bound to SANs/CN/root fingerprint; OIDC ID tokens; X5C signed-by-cert) / general-knowledge

option_description: Attests that enrollment tokens are cryptographically bound to the expected SAN/CN plus the CA root fingerprint (sub/sans/sha audience binding), so a captured token cannot be redirected to mint a cert for an arbitrary identity.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Provisioner / enrollment-token compromise" — fires when false: an unbound bearer token is a general-purpose issuance grant.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify tokens pin sub/sans plus the CA root SHA so they cannot be redirected to an arbitrary identity; unbound bearer tokens set this false.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {name,type}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm JWK/X5C tokens are bound (sub/sans/sha) to the expected identity + root fingerprint. Unbound bearer tokens = false.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (JWK token bound to SANs/CN/root fingerprint; OIDC ID tokens; X5C signed-by-cert) / general-knowledge

option_description: Attests the provisioner signing key / JWK provisioner password / OIDC trust material is access-controlled, stored in a secret manager, and rotated — not broadly shared. Theft lets an attacker mint trusted certs at will.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Provisioner / enrollment-token compromise" — fires when false (unprotected/broadly-shared key).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm provisioner signing key / JWK password / OIDC trust material is vaulted, access-controlled, and rotated, not broadly shared.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | {name,type}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verify provisioner key custody/rotation: key in a secret manager with access control and rotation = true; broadly-shared/static key = false.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (JWK token bound to SANs/CN/root fingerprint; OIDC ID tokens; X5C signed-by-cert) / general-knowledge

option_description: For OIDC provisioners, attests the ID token's iss/aud/exp claims are pinned and validated rather than treating a client secret as the only gate.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Provisioner / enrollment-token compromise" — fires when false: a token from the wrong issuer/audience or an expired token can drive issuance.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the OIDC provisioner pins and validates iss/aud/exp on the ID token rather than relying on a client secret alone.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[] | select(.type=="OIDC") | {name, clientID, configurationEndpoint, admins}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: OIDC provisioner pins issuer (configurationEndpoint) and clientID (aud) and enforces exp = true. Client-secret-only gating without claim pinning = false.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (JWK token bound to SANs/CN/root fingerprint; OIDC ID tokens; X5C signed-by-cert) / general-knowledge

option_description: Maximum validity (in days) a certificate issued by this enrollment flow may carry, mapped from the provisioner's maxTLSCertDuration (step-ca claims; default 24h). Bounding lifetime caps the blast radius of a mis-issuance or compromised key.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unbounded validity + missing revocation" — fires (HIGH_IS_INSECURE) above ~397 days (the CA/Browser-Forum leaf cap), and especially unbounded/multi-year durations up to the 3650-day max: a single mis-issued or stolen cert stays trusted for years.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the provisioner maxTLSCertDuration (and defaultTLSCertDuration) and express in days; confirm it is bounded and not overridable to years.
how_to_obtain.command: step ca provisioner list | jq '.[].claims | {minTLSCertDuration,maxTLSCertDuration,defaultTLSCertDuration,disableRenewal}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: maxTLSCertDuration e.g. "24h" (step-ca default), defaultTLSCertDuration "24h" — bounded (well below 397 days). Multi-year / unbounded = finding.
how_to_obtain.source: step-ca provisioners docs (minTLSCertDuration/maxTLSCertDuration/defaultTLSCertDuration claims)

option_description: Whether the enrollment flow's issued certificates carry a working revocation path (OCSP responder URI and/or CRL distribution point) so a mis-issued or compromised certificate can be recalled before natural expiry.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unbounded validity + missing revocation" — fires when false (no OCSP/CRL): combined with long validity, a bad certificate is trusted with no recall mechanism for years.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect an issued cert for an OCSP responder URI / CRL distribution point and verify the endpoint is reachable (or that validity is short enough to make revocation moot).
how_to_obtain.command: openssl x509 -in issued.pem -noout -ocsp_uri; dig +short CAA example.com
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Issued cert carries an OCSP URI / CRL DP (reachable), or validity is short enough to make revocation moot = true. Neither = false.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Private CA revocation docs (corpus: short-lived UsageMode reduces revocation dependence) / general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the enrollment flow enforces per-account / per-IP issuance rate limits (orders per window) with issuance-spike alerting. When false, a compromised credential or buggy client can flood the CA and mass-mint certificates unthrottled.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unmonitored / unthrottled issuance" — fires when false: unbounded issuance permits resource exhaustion and mass-minting from a compromised credential.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm per-account/per-IP issuance rate limits with spike alerting are configured on the enrollment endpoint (often at the reverse proxy, since step-ca OSS has limited built-in rate limiting).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Reverse-proxy / CA config attests issuance rate limits (orders per account/IP per window). step-ca OSS has limited built-in rate limiting — usually enforced at proxy; record where.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge / step-ca operational guidance

option_description: Whether every issuance is recorded in a structured, immutable audit log capturing provisioner, principal, requested vs issued SAN/Subject, serial, validity (notAfter), and challenge type.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unmonitored / unthrottled issuance" — fires when false: mis-issuance and provisioner abuse are undetectable and unattributable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm per-issuance records (provisioner, subject/SANs, serial, validity, challenge type) are present in the CA logs.
how_to_obtain.command: journalctl -u step-ca | grep -i 'sign\|provisioner\|certificate' | tail
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-issuance records with provisioner name, subject/SANs, serial, validity present (secure); silence = no audit trail (false).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge / step-ca operational guidance

option_description: Whether issuance audit records are shipped off-host to a SIEM / central log store rather than retained local-only and mutable. Local-only logs can be tampered with or wiped by an attacker who reaches the CA host.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unmonitored / unthrottled issuance" — fires when false: local-only mutable logs defeat detection of mis-issuance after a CA-host compromise.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm issuance audit records are forwarded off-host to a SIEM/central store rather than kept local-only and mutable.
how_to_obtain.command: journalctl -u step-ca | grep -i 'sign\|provisioner\|certificate' | tail
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Issuance records are exported to a SIEM/central store (verify a forwarder/shipper is configured and records arrive) = true; local-only retention = false.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge / step-ca operational guidance
